- issue_comment created in `venue-repo`#3 ("Figure and table widths and smallest type size of the venue") by `venue-repo`  > Answer for NeurIPS 2026 Main Track (sources in `VENUE.md` §4; style kit in `template/`):
  > 
  > - **Text block: 5.5 in × 9 in (396 pt wide), one column**, no two-column spanning. A figure placed at `\linewidth` is 5.5 in; never wider than the text block (no margin figures).
  > - **Body font:** Times (`ptm`), 10 pt on 11 pt; sans-serif Helvetica (`phv`). Match figure fonts to one of them, embedded (matplotlib `pdf.fonttype=42`); no Type 3.
  > - **Smallest type size:** the venue states **no minimum for text inside figures**; it only requires "neat, clean, and legible" artwork with dark lines. The style fixes `\footnotesize` = 8 pt, `\scriptsize` = 7 pt, `\tiny` = 6 pt and the body is 10 pt. My recommendation (not a venue rule): **7 pt at the placed width** for ticks/legend/panel labels, 8 pt for axis labels and table text. Your 7 pt placeholder is consistent with it; what matters is the size *after* placement at the width you declare in `\includegraphics`.
  > - **Colour:** allowed; captions and text must also be legible printed black/white, so add marker/linestyle differences, not colour alone.
  > - **Captions:** figure caption below, table caption above, sentence case, with the take-away message in the caption; tables with `booktabs`, no vertical rules; the style fixes the caption skips (7 pt).
  > - **Page limit:** 9 pages for the main text *including figures and tables*; references, appendix and the checklist do not count; no limit on appendix.
  > - **Count of figures/tables:** no venue limit. In 13 accepted main-track papers of this audience: figures median 4 (max 7), tables median 1 (max 6), together median 5 (max 9; sub-panels count as one figure). The outline's 5 figures + 3 tables is possible only if figures are compact: planning estimate 2.5–3.5 in of height per full-width multi-panel figure. Use up to 5 datasets × 4 models small multiples only if the panels still meet 7 pt at 5.5 in (≈ 5 columns of ≈ 1 in per panel). Else split to the appendix.
